clue.text: Big story created by someone going overboard

definitions.meaning: in newspaper jargon a sensational front-page story given prominent display
the noise and spray made when a person falls from a ship into the water

explanation.definitionFit: A splash is journalists' slang for a dominant front-page story, and also the sound of a body hitting water.

clue.text: Instrument never hard to play?

definitions.meaning: a keyboard instrument with hammers striking strings
the musical direction meaning softly, the opposite of loud or hard

explanation.walkthrough: The musical marking 'piano' tells players to play softly; the clue's 'never hard' is its playful paraphrase, with 'hard' standing in for 'loud'.
explanation.definitionFit: The keyboard instrument's name is the Italian marking for soft playing, the shortened form of pianoforte.

clue.text: Summing up about constant craving

indicators.note: about means one piece is placed around another, so the summing word encloses the letter

parts.note: summing up figures is addition
C is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot stop totting up figures has a persistent craving.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive dependence, an urge you cannot resist.

clue.text: Keen to export article from European country

indicators.note: to export is to send something out of a country, so a letter is sent out of the country's name

parts.note: Hungary is a country in central Europe
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A nation is eager to sell one of its goods abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungry for something means eager or avid for it.

clue.text: Tries boy in way that's characteristic of judges?

indicators.note: read as in a way, meaning the letters are put into some other order

explanation.surface: A lad is tried, and the court's conduct reflects judicial temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in way' tells you to rearrange TRIES and BOY together. The definition leans on the saying 'sober as a judge', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase sober as a judge makes seriousness and temperance a quality proverbially linked with the bench.

clue.text: Eat simple and honest scrambled eggs dish

indicators.note: scrambled means mixed up, so the letters of the three words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A cook urges you to eat plain, wholesome scrambled eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' looks like it belongs with 'eggs', but it is the anagram signal working on EAT, SIMPLE and HONEST ('and' is only a link).
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thick potato-and-egg tortilla from Spain, an egg-based dish.

clue.text: Opportunity and time for smashing result

parts.note: a break is a chance or opening, as in a lucky break
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Chance and timing combine to give a terrific outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakage is the damage left after something has been smashed.

clue.text: I make a killing as a whisky producer

parts.note: to slay is to kill

explanation.surface: A distiller boasts that he earns a fortune from whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a killing' suggests making lots of money, but here it is literal. ISLAY is a Scottish island famous for its malt whisky distilleries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebridean island hosts many distilleries, so it produces a great deal of Scotch.

clue.text: Skilled worker and master in new organisation

indicators.note: in a new organisation the letters are reorganised into a different order

explanation.surface: A craftsman and his boss join a newly formed company.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text had a stray 'I'; the printed clue anagrams AND and MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is a craftsman such as a plumber or electrician with practical training.

clue.text: It can be nominally replaced by union negotiation

definitions.text: It can be nominally replaced by union negotiation

parts.words: It can be nominally replaced by union negotiation
parts.note: the 'union' is a marriage, after which a bride often takes a new surname in place of the one she was born with

explanation.walkthrough: 'union negotiation' suggests trade-union bargaining, but the union is a wedding, and 'nominally' means as a matter of names.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's birth surname is often dropped for her husband's surname when she marries.

clue.text: Head's bloomer, perhaps

definitions.meaning: slang for the head or brain, as in use your noggin
a bloomer is a type of crusty bread, an example of a shaped baked item

explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder (a head's mistake), but it is a British bread. The 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang (loaf of bread for head) makes it the head; a bloomer is one shape of bread.

clue.text: Three notes used in musical compositions

parts.note: C is a musical note
a oncer is old British slang for a one-pound note
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A trio of notes recurs in a composer's works.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerti are pieces for soloist and orchestra, the Italian plural of concerto.

clue.text: Economist remaining when poet leaves town

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so the poet's name departs from the town's name

parts.note: Milton Keynes is a new town in Buckinghamshire, England
John Milton was the English poet of Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: An economist stays put after a poet departs a town.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was the influential British economist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Female dotty characters in Pacific republic

parts.note: lower-case i and j are the letters written with dots

explanation.surface: A mad woman's antics among South Sea islanders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dotty' looks like 'crazy', but it means letters bearing dots: i, j and i.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiji is an island nation in the South Pacific that became a republic in 1987.

clue.text: Foolish, as Dreyfus was?

definitions.meaning: Alfred Dreyfus, a French officer, was wrongly convicted of treason in 1894

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means unwise; read literally it describes someone wrongly sentenced by the court.

clue.text: In the event, this punishment is drastic

definitions.text: In the event, this punishment is drastic

parts.words: In the event, this punishment is drastic
parts.note: an athletics event at a track meeting, and the British idiom 'be for the' (this) meaning to face severe punishment

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the event' reads as 'as it turned out' but means 'as a sports event'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an athletics field event, and to be for it is British idiom for being in serious trouble.

clue.text: It might produce a situation giving patient man heart

parts.note: Job is the biblical figure proverbial for his patience
the heart of something is its centre

explanation.surface: Something gives a long-suffering man a new heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'situation' means a job vacancy: a JOBCENTRE is a UK government employment office.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jobcentre is the British state employment office that finds people work, a situation being a post.

clue.text: She can protect a man facing charges

definitions.text: She can protect a man facing charges

parts.words: She can protect a man facing charges
parts.note: a woman's name that is also the matador's slow cape pass, which shields him from the bull's rushes

explanation.walkthrough: 'facing charges' suggests a defendant in court; the charges are those of a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullfighting pass shares a girl's name, and the cape swing keeps the matador safe from the charging bull.

clue.text: It's skin is red and white, or orange

definitions.text: It's skin is red and white, or orange

parts.words: It's skin is red and white, or orange
parts.note: a spaniel breed with a red-and-white coat, and an orange-skinned English apple variety that both share a palace's name

explanation.walkthrough: The Blenheim spaniel is chestnut and white; the Blenheim Orange is a dessert apple, both named after Blenheim Palace in Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a red-and-white toy spaniel and a russet-gold apple are named after the Duke of Marlborough's Oxfordshire palace.

clue.text: Stop bribe

definitions.meaning: a stopper or plug for a cask
British slang for a backhander or illicit payment

explanation.definitionFit: A bung is a cask stopper, and in British slang a corrupt payment.

clue.text: Meeting requirement

parts.note: the minimum attendance needed before a meeting can do business

explanation.definitionFit: It is the minimum number of members needed for proceedings to be valid.

clue.text: Aggressive guy hits out, initially, with weapon

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the words guy, hits and out

explanation.surface: A violent man lashes out, armed with a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Gung-ho describes someone overly eager and belligerent.

clue.text: Author listeners might think is Sterne

indicators.note: listeners hear the clue word as a sound-alike, so it suggests what is heard rather than written

parts.note: said aloud, the novelist's name is 'stern', which means grim

explanation.surface: Readers mistake one writer for the eighteenth-century novelist Laurence Sterne.
explanation.walkthrough: Hear 'Sterne' as 'stern', meaning grim, which sounds like GRIMM, as in the Brothers Grimm.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm were the German collectors of fairy tales.

clue.text: Selected poet's line "of golden hue"

parts.note: aureate means golden or gilded

explanation.surface: A chosen poet's verse describes something golden.
explanation.walkthrough: A Poet Laureate is the poet chosen by the British monarch for the official post.
explanation.definitionFit: The Laureate is the poet appointed by the Crown, chosen for the honour.

clue.text: Reckon a pound is the full amount

parts.note: to tot up is to add up or reckon
L is the abbreviation for the pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone works out that a single pound is the entire sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the whole sum once everything is added.

clue.text: Fruit like a peach? Sounds just the opposite

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word must be heard rather than seen, so its spelling may differ

parts.note: the opposite of looking like a peach, a lovely sight, is unattractive or ugly

explanation.surface: A fruit is said to be peachy, though the name suggests otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like a peach' means beautiful; its opposite is UGLY, which is heard in UGLI, a lumpy Jamaican citrus.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a wrinkled Jamaican citrus, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: The American way — not willing to accept monarch

indicators.note: to accept means take in, so the monarch's letter is held inside

parts.note: intestate means dying without having made a will
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: The US approach is a refusal to recognise a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not willing' looks like reluctance but means without a will.
explanation.definitionFit: An interstate is a US highway linking states, a road being a way.

clue.text: A deal about what obstructs flow of water

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the deal encloses the obstruction

parts.note: a sale is a commercial deal
a dam blocks the flow of a river

explanation.surface: A bargain is struck over a barrage across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's ale is jokey old slang for plain water, since Adam had nothing else to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a humorous idiom for drinking water.

clue.text: Use mixed with milk, mostly, this food

indicators.note: mixed with means the letters are stirred together into a new order
mostly means most of the word but not all, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Instructions for a breakfast cereal: combine with milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims MILK to MIL, which is shuffled with USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a Swiss breakfast mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit.
